premise: After my mother died, I inherited her $350,000 farmhouse on 10 acres, but my brother—the executor and the golden child—forged a deed transferring it to himself for $1, claimed I had verbally agreed to sell, and evicted me on my 60th birthday; I hired a title attorney, proved the deed was a fabrication, and the court awarded me the house plus back rent, so now I lease the farmhouse back to him under a triple-net lease that rises each time he complains, while I live in the adjacent cottage running a farm-to-table B&B called ‘The Forged Acre’ with a permanent sign listing his criminal restitution case number.
